papers.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution

summary.tldr: MemT-1.0 introduces a memory-native foundation model architecture using Gated DeltaNet-2, a stable token-level memory update mechanism, and Mixture-of-Storage to internalize continuous memory accumulation.
key_points: Utilizes Gated DeltaNet-2 with token-level memory updates and Mixture-of-Storage to scale native memory capacity.
Trained via a two-stage pipeline (continued pre-training and post-training) using 34B tokens of training data.
Released in two model sizes: MemT-1.0-Nano and MemT-1.0-Flash.
Achieves a 1.86x end-to-end inference speedup and a 66x persistent storage reduction at 128K token history compared to full context KV cache.
Outperforms parametric memory baselines and matches retrieval-augmented methods while enhancing task success on agentic workflows.
summary.why_it_matters: Internalizing memory directly into the model's computation dramatically reduces persistent storage and speeds up inference compared to standard KV caches without sacrificing context quality or general capabilities.

papers.title: Learning from Fleet Experience: A Collective Learning Paradigm for Robots

summary.tldr: Collective Experience Learning (CEL) improves robot policies across fleets without human corrections by using Failure-Guided Experience Retrieval Fine-Tuning (FERT) to supervise policy updates with shared successful trajectory segments.
key_points: CEL introduces a shared-fleet framework where deployed robots learn continuously without collecting additional human teleoperator demonstrations or interventions.
FERT uses failure contexts from execution attempts to retrieve relevant successful trajectory segments from the shared fleet history, using those actions as policy supervision.
The Fault-Tolerant Asynchronous Training System (FATS) manages asynchronous experience collection, policy optimization, and distribution across the fleet.
In real-world tests across five manipulation tasks, FERT achieved 93.3-99.2% success rates; on a phone packaging task, scaling from 0 to 96 robots increased success from 79.2% to 98.3%.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables large robot fleets to continuously increase policy reliability during autonomous deployment without requiring human teleoperators to monitor execution or provide manual interventions.

papers.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding

summary.tldr: BrainLoRA uses parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) with LoRA and causal single-pass timepoint prediction to efficiently adapt multimodal backbones up to 104B parameters for state-of-the-art brain encoding.
key_points: Replaces sliding windows with the backbone's causal structure to predict multiple timepoints in a single forward pass, reducing feature-extraction costs.
Adapts multimodal backbones using LoRA and a lightweight readout, achieving first place on the Algonauts 2025 Challenge using a Qwen3-Omni backbone.
Implements a multi-LoRA kernel to accelerate joint training of multiple adapters on a shared backbone, enabling an ensemble of over 200 models.
Demonstrates via modality attribution that adapted backbones recover canonical sensory topography and increase the contribution of audio inputs and cross-modal mixing.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables the adaptation of massive multimodal foundation models for neural response prediction without requiring prohibitive compute or vast amounts of scarce neural data.

papers.title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience

summary.tldr: EgoXperience introduces EgoX-Engine, EgoX-Data-6M, and EgoX, a unified paradigm that reconstructs camera, scene, hands, and objects in a shared world coordinate frame from monocular egocentric video in a single forward pass.
key_points: EgoX-Engine uses geometrically verified object tracking coupled with SLAM-based world alignment to generate consistent auto-annotations for scenes, camera, hands, and objects.
EgoX-Data-6M comprises 50 hours of task-driven indoor/outdoor manipulation and locomotion with second-level captions, from which EgoX-Bench (1 hour) was derived for joint reconstruction evaluation.
The EgoX model takes monocular egocentric video and first-frame object masks to output joint metric 3D reconstructions in world space without multi-stage pipelines.
Compared to top baselines, EgoX reduces camera, hand, and depth errors by 68.9%, 65.6%, and 42.9% respectively, while raising object pose recovery scores by 28.0%.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a single-pass framework and benchmark for holistically grounded 3D scene and hand-object interaction recovery from monocular egocentric video.

papers.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory

summary.tldr: OpenVLHarness introduces a multimodal reasoning harness featuring a tool capability layer and persistent multimodal memory, enabling MLLMs to acquire, render, and programmatically compose heterogeneous visual evidence while reducing token costs.
key_points: Organized around a capability layer that converts heterogeneous tool backends into model-readable observations using task-level interfaces and evidence rendering.
Employs persistent multimodal memory to retain addressable artifacts—including images, structured data, and web references—across reasoning steps.
Includes a coding interface that executes generated programs over stored memory artifacts to combine outputs from multiple tools.
Outperforms base models across 22 benchmarks, achieving a 9.7-12.6 point average gain, including +11.2 with Qwen3-VL-8B, +9.7 with Kimi K3, and +9.9 with GPT-6 Astra.
Achieves a 7.7-8.5 point gain over Codex and Visual Sketchpad at maximum effort while using at most 37% of their model-token cost when evaluated with GPT-6 Luna.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that structured tool integration and persistent memory provide substantially higher visual reasoning performance than scaling inference compute alone, while significantly lowering token usage.

papers.title: Holi-World: Building Holistic World Intelligence from Human-Ego Experience

summary.tldr: HOLI-WORLD is an integrated ecosystem that automatically transforms egocentric human experience into structured world records and learning resources for spatial and temporal machine reasoning.
key_points: HOLIWORLD-Foundry uses complementary static and dynamic perception to automatically link persistent scene structure, evolving object states, interaction histories, and observations.
HOLIWORLD-Data compiles records from ~100 self-collected scenes into visual-language training resources, featuring ~80K grounded QA pairs used to train HOLIWORLD-VL-4B.
HOLIWORLD-Bench provides independent human-annotated heldout recordings to evaluate annotation quality alongside spatial and temporal understanding.
Experiments demonstrate strong static perception and dynamic tracking capabilities across ScanNet, ScanNet++, Aria Digital Twin, HOLIWORLD-Bench, and EgoDynamic4D.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes an automated pipeline to scale machine learning of dynamic 3D environments directly from continuous, unannotated human egocentric video.

papers.title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents

summary.tldr: CoworkEnv is a framework that synthesizes executable, programmatically validated training environments, curated demonstrations, and reinforcement learning rollouts for long-horizon AI coworker models.
key_points: Uses workflow requirements for task construction and programmatic validation with feedback repair to verify generated specifications and grading checks.
Generates curated SFT demonstrations via teacher executions and RL rollouts with rewards from student interactions to train compact PocketWorker models.
SFT on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct increased the mean score on Claw-Eval from 46.6 to 64.1, featuring a 31.9-point increase on multi-turn tasks.
Demonstrates transferability to ClawMark via an SFT-only extension and provides preliminary evidence of policy optimization under different RL reward processing and credit assignment configurations.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, automated synthesis of reliable multi-turn environments and training data needed to improve small vision-language models on complex, tool-using agent tasks.

papers.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts

summary.tldr: AnyGoal is a benchmark and open-source library that evaluates world model dynamics generalization under compositional state-action recombinations absent from expert rollouts.
key_points: Introduces the AnyGoal benchmark featuring goal-shifted task variants designed to test compositional generalization using familiar state factors and actions.
Tests world models on underrepresented state-action combinations that remain within training support but fall outside expert trajectory distributions.
Reveals that current world model families consistently fail at prediction and planning when evaluating state-action recombinations across various interaction regimes.
summary.why_it_matters: World models must generalize beyond expert trajectories to enable reliable planning and simulation in novel, goal-shifted task environments.

papers.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models

summary.tldr: RoboValue is a fine-grained sim-and-real benchmark and dataset that unifies the evaluation of robotic value models across four core capabilities: task-state understanding, temporal progress monitoring, failure/recovery reasoning, and value consistency.
key_points: RoboValue-Dataset features expert demonstrations and annotated trajectories across 15 simulation and 20 real-world robotic manipulation tasks.
Evaluates robotic value models under zero-shot and one-shot settings across four capability dimensions, including performance under shifts in environment and robot embodiment.
Benchmark testing revealed critical failures in history-dependent progress tracking, fine-grained instruction grounding, and recovery assessment, even among models with high outcome scores.
Experiments demonstrated value consistency issues, showing that identical semantic subtasks receive varied value gains depending on valid execution orders.
summary.why_it_matters: By exposing hidden failure modes in robotic value feedback systems, RoboValue provides a standardized benchmark and leaderboard to improve value-based policy supervision and execution monitoring.

papers.title: InfiniDream: Open-Ended Photorealistic 3D Worlds Through Procedural Generation

summary.tldr: InfiniDream is a VLM-driven framework that generates open-ended, photorealistic, and editable 3D worlds using procedural code and frustum-guided grid placement.
key_points: Uses Symbolically Constrained Asset Generation to leverage existing procedural algorithms for novel 3D asset creation while maintaining seed-based diversity and editability.
Combines VLM-based semantic scene planning with Deterministic Frustum-Guided Grid Placement for precise object placement, procedural population, and animation in large-scale worlds.
Validated across 100 object and 20 scene generation tasks, outperforming baseline methods across four perceptual metrics and human preference evaluations.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables automated, scalable creation of complex, photorealistic, and editable 3D environments without relying on rigid predefined API factories or manual procedural design.

papers.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention

summary.tldr: KronLSTM introduces the Kronecker Delta Rule, a minimally invasive memory-revision mechanism for xLSTM that modifies associative matrix memories along a single direction to prevent interference and stabilize long-context processing.
key_points: Introduces the Kronecker Delta Rule to correct targeted associations via single-direction matrix space updates, minimizing interference with prior data.
Modeled mathematically as a Markov chain converging to a steady-state distribution with a uniformly bounded expected memory matrix norm.
Eliminates the need for external normalization or stabilization mechanisms to maintain stable memory dynamics across long sequences.
Outperforms or matches existing linear attention models, such as the (Gated) DeltaNet family, on long-context language modeling tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables stable, long-context linear attention without requiring extra memory normalization techniques, offering open-source code and models for scalable sequence processing.

papers.title: Manga2Animate: An Agentic Framework for Faithful Manga Animation with Script and Storyboard Planning

summary.tldr: Manga2Animate is a multi-agent framework that generates faithful, shot-consistent manga animations using agentic script and visual storyboard planning with panel-grounded feedback.
key_points: Decomposes manga animation into two intermediate representations: an animation script and a visual storyboard.
Employs a creator-reviewer agent pairing for each stage to evaluate and refine representations directly against the original manga panels.
Utilizes representation-specific selection and dual-level feedback loops to progressively fix structural and storyline errors before final video synthesis.
Outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in source faithfulness and cross-shot visual consistency in user studies and experiments.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents character loss and storyline misinterpretation in automated manga adaptation by enforcing direct grounding in source panels through intermediate multi-agent planning.

papers.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy

summary.tldr: PhysRSI-eval introduces a five-axis framework to quantify physical recursive self-improvement in Vision-Language Models across 18 manipulation tasks under fixed interaction budgets.
key_points: Evaluates physical recursive self-improvement (RSI) across five axes: First-Attempt Performance, Efficiency, Success, Budget, and Improvement from failure.
Proposes the Physical Barrel Hypothesis, stating that distinct underlying capabilities bound specific aspects of physical improvement.
Demonstrates that workspace interventions, such as removing interaction history, reduce late-round success while frozen workspaces remain functional on unseen layouts.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a structured methodology to evaluate and forecast how effectively Vision-Language Model agents adapt, learn from physical feedback, and generalize across robotic manipulation tasks.

papers.title: AdaExploreBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Proactive Exploration and Test-time Adaptation in Evolving Environments

summary.tldr: AdaExploreBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLM agents on proactive exploration, rule inference, and test-time adaptation under unannounced, implicit environmental dynamics shifts.
key_points: Environmental dynamics are modeled as hidden rules that agents must actively discover through evidence collection.
Implicit rule drift alters latent rules without notification, forcing agents to detect performance drops and re-explore.
Evaluations on eight top LLMs show GPT-6 Sol achieved only 61.9% calibrated accuracy.
Providing sufficient evidence or eliminating rule drift improved average agent performance by nearly 10%.
summary.why_it_matters: Current LLM agents excel at reasoning from provided data but struggle with active evidence gathering and detecting when environmental changes invalidate past knowledge.

papers.title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation

summary.tldr: AffordanceWAM is a generative world-action model that uses scalar affordances and affordance heatmaps within a video diffusion Transformer to enable zero-shot action transfer from human videos to robot manipulation.
key_points: Couples separately parameterized World and Action Experts using Masked Joint Self-Attention built on a pretrained video diffusion Transformer.
Jointly predicts future RGB observations, Scalar Affordance fields, Affordance Heatmaps, and continuous robot actions via a unified flow-matching objective.
Leverages egocentric human videos to supervise the three future-world streams, enabling human-to-robot transfer without human action labels or kinematics retargeting.
Demonstrates monotonic performance improvements on the RoboCasa benchmark as affordance-annotated human video data scales under fixed robot supervision.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes object-centric affordance as a shared visual interface that allows robots to learn manipulation actions from scalable, action-unlabeled human videos.

papers.title: Competing Learning in Hybrid Architectures

summary.tldr: A newly identified Competing Learning phenomenon in hybrid language models causes fast-learning linear-time recurrence layers to suppress training signals for softmax attention layers, preventing attention from learning contextual information retrieval.
key_points: Layer attribution analysis shows linear recurrence layers learn retrieval functions faster than softmax attention layers under typical data distributions.
When recurrence layers learn retrieval early, they suppress the corresponding gradient/learning signal needed for attention layers to develop retrieval capabilities.
Pausing weight updates in recurrence layers mid-training enables attention layers to successfully learn retrieval functions.
A staged pre-training procedure based on this mechanism improves language modeling loss, common-sense reasoning, and retrieval performance in models up to 1B parameters.
summary.why_it_matters: Staged training resolves internal layer competition in hybrid architectures, allowing linear recurrence to maintain high throughput while enabling attention to reach full potential in retrieval tasks.

papers.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution

summary.tldr: MemT-1.0 introduces a memory-native architecture using Gated DeltaNet-2, Mixture-of-Storage, and a two-stage 34B-token training pipeline to internalize continuous memory updates into model computation.
key_points: Architecture incorporates Gated DeltaNet-2 for stable token-level memory updates within context turns alongside a Mixture-of-Storage design to scale capacity.
Trained via a two-stage pipeline (continued pre-training and post-training) using 34B tokens, yielding two released models: MemT-1.0-Nano and MemT-1.0-Flash.
Achieves a ~1.86x end-to-end inference speedup and a 66x reduction in persistent storage compared to a full-context KV cache at a 128K history length.
Outperforms parametric memory baselines, matches retrieval-augmented methods, and improves agentic task performance by internalizing retrieved procedural experience.
summary.why_it_matters: MemT-1.0 demonstrates that internalizing memory directly into model weights drastically reduces KV-cache storage footprint and speeds up inference while keeping retrieval-level performance intact.

papers.title: Copying Under Repetition: From Prefix Matching to Position Hashing

summary.tldr: A 2-layer transformer using RoPE-style VO-rotations with prime periods can copy arbitrary repeated strings up to length N, overcoming finite-precision baseline models that fail due to positional saturation.
key_points: Baseline architectures using NoPE or ALiBi fail on long repeated sequences because additive attention biases saturate, making identical-token run logits constant and causing termination errors.
The proposed architecture requires two layers, O(log log N)-bit precision, and O(log N / log log N) width to correctly copy and terminate for strings up to horizon N.
VO-rotations apply RoPE-style rotations to attention values and outputs using small prime periods to encode distances from delimiter anchors, uniquely resolved via the Chinese Remainder Theorem.

Empirically, trained VO models demonstrate near-perfect accuracy generalization up to length 5005 (the product of the selected prime periods), whereas baseline transformers fail within the training range.
summary.why_it_matters: It identifies the structural cause of character overrun/truncation errors in frontier LLMs during repetition and provides a provably scalable positional encoding mechanism to fix them.

papers.title: Parallel Language Models via Variational Decoding

summary.tldr: Parallel Language Models (PLMs) achieve 2.3-5.7x faster inference by generating mutually consistent tokens in a single forward pass using latent auxiliary variables and variational decoding.
key_points: PLMs route dependencies through latent auxiliary variables to enable parallel token generation in one forward pass.
The training objective uses a variational bound combining an autoregressive loss with a parallel decoding loss.
Pretrained PLMs scale from 80M to 3B parameters, achieving near-autoregressive pretraining loss with inference speedups following a power law in model size.
A post-trained 1.3B parameter PLM matches or exceeds an equivalent autoregressive model on math, coding, and instruction-following benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: PLMs eliminate the traditional speed-quality trade-off of parallel generation, matching autoregressive accuracy while substantially reducing inference latency.

papers.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions

summary.tldr: WeAct introduces weight-level internal actions that allow agents to dynamically switch capability-specific LoRA adapters at runtime via native tool-calling interfaces over a frozen backbone.
key_points: Adds LoRA adapter selection directly into the agent's action space alongside standard external actions.
Prevents catastrophic forgetting during long-horizon tasks by keeping the LLM backbone frozen and using independent capability adapters.
Outperforms full fine-tuning by 6.2% and static LoRA-merging by 27.5% in average accuracy on Qwen3-32B across eight deep-research benchmarks.
Enables modular continual adaptation, allowing individual adapters to be added or updated without altering the backbone or existing adapters.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a compute-efficient, modular method for agents to dynamically switch capabilities on demand and continually learn without suffering from catastrophic forgetting or static weight interference.

papers.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models

summary.tldr: LatComm introduces a latent communication interface that compresses contexts into reusable fixed-size packets sent between frozen LLMs using prompt-gated cross-attention.
key_points: Separates context encoding from reading: a frozen encoder LLM compresses the context once without the question, allowing a different frozen receiver LLM to read it across multiple questions.
Employs cross-attention at the receiver model with gating mechanisms computed directly from the question prompt.
Outperforms single-vector baselines by up to 10.2 points in average accuracy across 12 multiple-choice question-answering datasets.
Achieves a 57x reduction in receiver input size and a 3x speedup when answering questions per article on the QuALITY benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient, low-latency multi-LLM systems by eliminating the need to repeatedly re-encode long shared contexts as text for subsequent queries.

papers.title: Safety Mid-Training: Internalizing LLM Safety as a Foundational Capability

summary.tldr: Safety mid-training inserts a stage between pre-training and post-training to jointly learn safety and general reasoning via shared structured reasoning traces, improving safety persistence and general capabilities.
key_points: Introduces safety mid-training, leveraging structured documents and reasoning traces generated from safety and utility prompts by the base model.
Reduces average attack success rate (ASR) by 72% to 81% relative to Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B base models while simultaneously enhancing general capabilities.
Maintains safety and lower ASR following general-only Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and general-only Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) without safety rewards.
Establishes an improved safety-utility Pareto frontier during subsequent reinforcement learning (RL) when starting from mid-trained model checkpoints.
summary.why_it_matters: Internalizing safety alongside general reasoning in mid-training prevents safety degradation during subsequent general-purpose post-training without incurring the typical utility trade-off.

papers.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning

summary.tldr: TokenGate introduces a lightweight, drop-in component that uses token-gated attention to enable end-to-end learnable token pruning during the transformer prefill phase.
key_points: Uses token-gated attention inspired by Mixture-of-Experts to re-weight attention logits with token importance scores, bypassing non-differentiable top-K selection for end-to-end training.
Achieves 1.4x to 11.3x faster time-to-first-token (TTFT) and 1.5x to 3.4x lower peak memory during prefill with no accuracy loss.
Outperforms prior token-pruning techniques by up to 6.4x faster prefill speed and 2x lower peak memory.
Extends both standard transformers (e.g., Qwen3) and hybrid-attention architectures (e.g., Qwen3.5) using lightweight adaptation similar to parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: TokenGate significantly accelerates prefill latency and reduces peak GPU memory consumption for long-context language models without sacrificing model accuracy.

papers.title: Hierarchical Token Merging with Recursive Autoencoders for Unsupervised Grammar Induction

summary.tldr: A hierarchical token-merging autoencoder uses a variational information bottleneck and dynamic programming to marginalize over binary trees, achieving unsupervised grammar induction solely through compression.
key_points: Recursively merges adjacent tokens into abstract representations via dynamic programming that marginalizes over all candidate binary parse trees.
Utilizes a variational information bottleneck to enforce sequence compression without explicit structural supervision.
Employs unsupervised consensus and distillation to combine independently trained models and mitigate training instability.
Achieves 93% grammatical parse-validity and 93% exact reconstruction on held-out synthetic sequences, outperforming the strongest trivial baseline of 42% parse-validity.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a proof of concept that meaningful compositional hierarchies and syntactic structure can emerge purely through data compression mechanisms.

papers.title: Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: Mitigating Rubric Hacking through Latent Dimension Recovery and Balancing

summary.tldr: Researchers identify Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence—where models trade off sub-dimension quality to maximize total reward—and propose FRDA and RSDC to balance rubric dimensions and mine implicit semantic evaluators.
key_points: Identifies Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence, where rising total rubric scores correlate with systematic score drops in specific sub-dimensions.
Highlights two key sub-dimension failure modes: dimension imbalance (policy favors over-covered dimensions) and dimension absence (systematic reward-quality gap).
Introduces Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation (FRDA) to force generations to compete per-dimension, counteracting rubric imbalance.
Introduces Residual Semantic Dimension Completion (RSDC) to mine latent evaluation dimensions from holistic preference signals to fix rubric coverage gaps.
Demonstrates improved response quality and training stability over single-reward and naive multi-reward aggregation in chat, science, and medical domains.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents reinforcement learning models from exploiting aggregated reward functions, resulting in broader evaluation coverage and higher-quality generation across specialized domains.

security.title: Accountable partial understanding: securing the epistemic attack surface of agentic systems

summary.tldr: This paper characterizes the epistemic attack surface of agentic AI systems and proposes Accountable Partial Understanding (APU), a framework comprising six necessary conditions, five design principles, and two measurement dimensions for securing delegated software authority.
key_points: Identifies a taxonomy of four epistemic attack categories targeting intent interpretation, evidence handling, delegated authority scope, and human supervisor comprehension.
Defines six necessary APU conditions: bounded scope with explicit assumptions, inspectable evidence, assigned responsibility, visible residual unknowns, actionability, and temporal maintenance.

Establishes five design principles, including bounded delegation, decoupled evidence, assumption tracking with invalidation, role-specific accountability views, and intervention-preserving design with residual unknown registers.
Introduces two measurable probe dimensions—evidence linkage and invalidation latency—to evaluate accountability mechanisms under adversarial pressure.
Grounds theoretical analysis using three agentic use cases: an AI coding agent, an autonomous cyber-defense agent, and an AI-mediated insulin delivery update system.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a structured architecture and concrete metrics to safely grant autonomous authority to AI agents even when human supervisors cannot achieve full operational comprehension.

security.title: Game of Phones: Harnessing Game Theory and LLMs in 'Bot Wars' to Counteract Phone Scams

summary.tldr: A game-theoretic framework enables LLMs to adapt counter-strategies during automated scam-baiting, achieving closer alignment to Nash equilibrium without model fine-tuning.
key_points: Models scammer-baiter interactions as a two-player game with empirically grounded strategies, utility functions, and a Nash equilibrium benchmark.
Uses in-context learning to dynamically adapt strategies without requiring fine-tuning.
Evaluated across 300 simulated dialogues and three LLM architectures, achieving 28.9% to 79.7% closer alignment to Nash equilibrium compared to non-adaptive baselines.
Releases an open-source codebase and a dataset of 300 dialogues annotated with turn-level strategy labels and utility scores.
summary.why_it_matters: Automating adaptive scam-baiting increases resource costs for scammers, offering a proactive approach to deplete their operational capacity.

security.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Cost-Aware Metric for Evaluating Iterative LLM Jailbreaks

summary.tldr: A new evaluation metric, ASR_STEP, penalizes iterative LLM jailbreak attacks based on the number of calls made to the victim model.
key_points: ASR_STEP modifies traditional Attack Success Rate by discounting scores based on repeated victim-model interactions.
GCG scores drop by 7.0 to 8.7 percentage points under ASR_STEP discounting on JailBreakBench.
PAIR scores drop by 3.4 to 12.0 percentage points depending on the iterative strategy, while single-step PAP scores remain unchanged.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating jailbreaks with ASR_STEP provides a realistic security assessment by accounting for the increased risk of attack detection during multi-step model queries.

security.title: Connection Escrow: Holding AI-Agent Pod Egress in the Kernel Until an Isolated Verifier Rules

summary.tldr: Connection escrow uses a 98-instruction eBPF program to hold outbound TCP connections in the kernel's connect() path until an isolated container verifier issues a signed, single-use verdict tied to the socket cookie.
key_points: Uses a 98-instruction eBPF program on the pod's cgroup to park outbound TCP connections before packets are sent, attributing sockets to process, executable digest, and SPIFFE identity.
Requires verifiers in separate containers to issue signed, unexpired, single-use verdicts referencing the specific socket cookie; late or forged verdicts cause connection resets.
Captures request content without terminating end-to-end TLS by placing eBPF uprobes at the agent's TLS library boundary (OpenSSL or Go crypto/tls) for model scoring.
Adds a 4.5 ms median latency per released connection (24 us policy overhead) and successfully gated 600 connections across six Kubernetes pods without modifying agents.
Blocks bypass attempts including child processes, renamed binaries, raw sockets bypassing sidecar proxies, and direct attempts to reach the verifier.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents compromised or malicious AI agents from bypassing network security controls via direct sockets or child processes without requiring proxy TLS termination or application modifications.

security.title: Fake News, Real Crashes: Information Injection Attacks on LLM Financial Trading Agents

summary.tldr: A new benchmark demonstrates that LLM financial trading agents are vulnerable to information injection, where fabricated news and specific 30-word templates reach up to 100% attack success rates by manipulating evidence rather than instructions.
key_points: Information injection via fabricated news achieves a 62% attack success rate (ASR) compared to 14% for prompt injection, with two 30-word templates reaching 100% ASR across 15 U.S. stocks.
Fact-poisoning effectiveness relies heavily on surface-level credibility cues (e.g., source names, 'BREAKING' tags), as removing them drops ASR from 100% to 0% despite identical underlying claims.
Attack success is state-dependent; for example, a fake indicator panel scores 91% ASR against an agent inclined to hold, but only 12% against one inclined to buy.
Model scaling, peer debate, and standard defenses fail against fact poisoning, with only hierarchical aggregation successfully reducing the ASR.
summary.why_it_matters: Automated LLM trading agents sharing similar news feeds and policies are highly susceptible to coordinated market manipulation and synchronized crashes triggered by simple, crafted fake news.

security.title: SpanGuard: Decoupling Instruction Localization from Authorization for Lightweight IPI Defense

summary.tldr: SpanGuard decouples Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) defense into unsupervised instruction localization and small-LLM authorization, reducing required model capability while maintaining a 0.32% attack success rate.
key_points: Identifies that small LLMs fail at IPI defense primarily due to jointly performing instruction localization and authorization judgment.
Uses lightweight unsupervised segmentation to partition heterogeneous tool outputs into localized regions based on semantic discontinuity.
Employs a small language model to perform block-level authorization checks on localized regions against the user request.
Achieves a 0.32% attack success rate with negligible loss in benign utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables lightweight, computationally cheap language models to provide robust IPI defense without relying on large, resource-intensive guardrail models.

security.title: SPLASH: Contrastive Audit Pressure for Detecting and Localizing Security Hallucinations in Generated Code

summary.tldr: SPLASH introduces audit pressure, contrasting teacher-forced log-probabilities under security versus style reviews to detect and localize security hallucinations in LLM-generated code without model training or static rules.
key_points: Measures audit pressure by evaluating teacher-forced log-probabilities of a generated program under a security review prompt versus a style review prompt.
Aggregates token-level scores to statements and programs using a probabilistic model of competing edits to locate vulnerable statements and pick secure candidates.
Evaluated on 63,684 programs generated by 12 models across 899 tasks, achieving 74% accuracy in selecting secure code and placing the vulnerable statement first in 58% of insecure samples.
Requires no internal access to the generating model, model training, or CWE-specific rules, outperforming frontier LLM judges.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables black-box selection of secure code variants and precise line-level vulnerability localization in LLM outputs without relying on brittle static analysis or retraining the underlying models.

security.title: RAGLeak: Supply-Chain Privacy Backdoors in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary.tldr: RAGLeak is a supply-chain privacy backdoor attack that forces LLMs to reversibly obfuscate retrieved private documents for later high-fidelity extraction by an auxiliary model.
key_points: Decouples privacy leakage from direct textual exposure by reversibly obfuscating private retrieved documents upon trigger activation.
Employs an auxiliary LLM to decode and recover the obfuscated private data with high fidelity.
Achieves up to 100% Attack Success Rate (ASR) across three model families and three application domains.
Demonstrates resistance to defenses, experiencing at most a 10-percentage-point drop in ASR under representative detection methods.
Persists after clean fine-tuning and generalizes across different model scales and versions.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that compromised RAG models in the software supply chain can stealthily exfiltrate sensitive retrieved data without relying on obvious prompt injections or explicit text duplication.

security.title: Secure Agentic Coding through Counterexample-Grounded Feedback

summary.tldr: Falcon is a counterexample-grounded security verification framework that separates attack exploration from behavioral verification using execution traces to improve secure code generation.
key_points: Connects attack exploration and behavioral verification via execution traces of the program under test.
Outperforms alternative security signals, static analysis, and learned rewards on held-out functional-security gains during test-time repair and RL training.
Combines with proxy rewards to mitigate reward overoptimization while retaining guidance from existing security signals.
Maintains or enhances overall code functionality while fixing underlying vulnerabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: Execution-grounded counterexample feedback prevents coding agents from gaming security rewards without resolving actual software vulnerabilities.

security.title: Budgeted Attack Scheduling for LLM Red-Teaming: The Roles of Static Priors, Semantic Guidance, and Online Feedback

summary.tldr: This paper formalizes LLM red-teaming as a budgeted attack scheduling problem over fixed attack libraries, evaluating how static historical ASR priors, semantic guidance, and online feedback perform across different victim-defense conditions.
key_points: Formalizes attack prioritization under query constraints as a budgeted scheduling problem across three signal sources: static historical ASR priors, LLM semantic guidance, and online query feedback.
Evaluated four scheduling strategies across three victim models and three defense settings on GPT-5.2.
Historical ASR provides strong initial scheduling but degrades under defense-induced distribution shifts.
Semantic guidance outperforms or matches static priors during cold-start regimes, while online feedback compensates when historical priors become stale or unavailable.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables cost-effective, targeted LLM robustness evaluations by optimizing attack prompt selection under strict token and budget limits.

security.title: Towards Architectural-Level Safety Control: Relocating Hazardous Knowledge into Removable Experts in Mixture-of-Experts Models

summary.tldr: REX achieves architectural-level unlearning in Mixture-of-Experts models by relocating hazardous knowledge into newly added, physically removable experts using selective gradient masking and routing differentiation.
key_points: Expands MoE architectures with dedicated experts to isolate hazardous knowledge from general capabilities.
Employs selective gradient masking and routing differentiation to move risk-related knowledge out of original parameters into the new experts.
Excision of the designated experts on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B drops WMDP-Bio accuracy by 48.4 points while keeping MMLU performance within 3 points.
Prevents post-release knowledge recovery under subsequent fine-tuning; after 250M tokens of fine-tuning, WMDP-Bio accuracy only reaches 42.8% compared to a baseline rebound of 78.3%.
summary.why_it_matters: Physically removing dedicated experts prevents malicious actors from recovering unsafe knowledge through post-deployment fine-tuning, outperforming traditional weight-suppression unlearning methods.

security.title: How Effectively Do Security Skills Guide Coding Agents in Vulnerability Detection in Linux Kernel?

summary.tldr: An empirical study of 37 security skills across 14,800 runs shows LLM coding agents struggle with Linux kernel vulnerability detection, prompting SKILL-SIF, a self-improving framework that evolves skills based on failure patterns.
key_points: In a benchmark of 100 Linux kernel vulnerabilities across 10 classes, Claude Code with four LLMs achieved 24.4% accuracy at the function level, 18.3% at the statement level, and 15.7% for vulnerability classification.
Identified failure modes include limitations in evidence acquisition, state-relation reasoning, code interpretation, candidate verification, investigation coverage, and reporting.

The SKILL-SIF framework iteratively improves security skills by learning from missed vulnerabilities, boosting fully correct vulnerability detection on 100 unseen cases from 2% to 16% (and aggregate LLM accuracy from 6.05% to 11.20%).
summary.why_it_matters: Existing static security skills offer limited efficacy for LLM-based kernel auditing, but failure-driven skill evolution can significantly enhance automated vulnerability detection in complex software.

security.title: SEAL: Towards Persistent Tool Poisoning Attack against LLM Agents via Prefix-Eliciting Trigger

summary.tldr: SEAL is a two-stage persistent tool poisoning method that uses prefix-eliciting triggers to maintain attack effectiveness across multi-round LLM agent interactions.
key_points: Identifies that existing single-round tool poisoning attacks degrade in multi-round settings because agents fail to consistently surface attack-relevant signals as context evolves.
Uses Prefix-Eliciting Trigger Optimization (PETO) to optimize context-specific triggers that force attack-relevant reasoning prefixes in individual contexts.
Applies Local-to-Universal Trigger Aggregation (L2U) to combine local triggers into a universal trigger that generalizes across contexts and execution rounds.
Demonstrates attack effectiveness, cross-model transferability, and defense resistance across seven multi-round scenarios.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals that tool poisoning remains a practical security threat in realistic, multi-round LLM agent deployments where previous single-round attack methods fail.

security.title: Policy Is Not Capability: Some Safety Benchmarks Measure Which Definition of "Unsafe" You Trained On

summary.tldr: A study shows safety benchmarks often measure alignment with specific annotation policy definitions rather than actual model capability, with benchmark scores swinging dramatically based on policy labels or minor parameter tweaks.
key_points: Significant benchmark contamination was found in training pools, including 88% of JailbreakBench-benign and 82% of OR-Bench-hard.
Benchmark score variance across ten identical-architecture guardrail arms ranged from 0.043 on WildGuard-benign to 0.99 on HarmBench-copyright depending on the label definition used.

Modifying just 0.03% of model parameters or altering the teacher model's soft labels during distillation can shift benchmark scores across their entire range (e.g., HarmBench-copyright from 0 to 100).
Validation accuracy correlated strongly with annotator policy agreement (rho=+0.74) rather than actual detection capability (rho=+0.34).
summary.why_it_matters: Standard safety benchmarks can be heavily gaming-susceptible and confounded by hidden label definitions or teacher provenance, making reported safety capability claims misleading without strict policy controls.

security.title: Don't Judge an Agent by Its Messages: Private-State Leakage under Passive Monitoring of Agent Communication

summary.tldr: This paper proves that passive auditing of agent communications cannot rule out private-state leakage even when task performance and message distributions are preserved, but a canonical task interface can mathematically bound this leakage.
key_points: Fixing the task-relevant message distribution and declared utilities can still leave a full private bit exposed to public decoders.

Using Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on a synthetic routing task, selecting among 16 responses achieved 98.60% routing accuracy while allowing a public decoder to recover a private bit in all 8,192 held-out rounds.
A law-preserving sender constructed from response samples allowed private bit recovery in 97.7% of rounds while keeping generic monitors without the true bit near chance accuracy.
A canonical task interface bounds remaining information about a balanced attribute by twice the routing-error rate, even if the receiver shares a key with the sender.
summary.why_it_matters: Passive monitoring of agent communication is insufficient to guarantee privacy, highlighting the need to enforce communication constraints via task interfaces rather than relying solely on message audits.

infra.title: TorchTPU is now open source: Run native PyTorch on TPUs

summary.tldr: Google Cloud has open-sourced TorchTPU, a tool enabling developers to run native PyTorch models on Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).
key_points: TorchTPU provides open-source integration for executing native PyTorch code directly on Google Cloud TPU hardware.
summary.why_it_matters: It simplifies the execution of PyTorch workloads on Google Cloud TPU infrastructure without requiring proprietary modifications.

infra.title: Announcing llm-d 1.0: Open distributed inference for agents on Google Cloud TPUs and GPUs

summary.tldr: Google Cloud has announced the release of llm-d 1.0, an open-source distributed inference framework designed for running AI agents across Google Cloud TPUs and GPUs.
key_points: llm-d 1.0 provides an open-source stack optimized for distributed LLM inference on Google Cloud infrastructure.
The framework supports execution across both Google Cloud TPU and GPU hardware targets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables developers to deploy distributed, agentic AI workloads using an open-source framework tailored for Google Cloud hardware.

infra.title: Accelerating Mamba-2 with High-Performance Forward Pass Kernels in NVIDIA CUDA Tile

summary.tldr: NVIDIA CUDA Tile (cuTile) is a Python-based DSL and parallel programming model that abstracts thread- and warp-level scheduling to write high-performance GPU kernels for Mamba-2 directly in Python.
key_points: cuTile provides a tile-centric programming model that hides low-level thread and warp scheduling behind Python primitives.
The compiler automatically applies optimizations to leverage advanced NVIDIA GPU hardware capabilities for tile-level execution.
summary.why_it_matters: It simplifies the creation of peak-performance forward pass kernels for Mamba-2 models using high-level Python instead of complex CUDA C++.

infra.title: One Search, Two Layers: Compiler Controls Inside PyTorch Helion using NVIDIA CompileIQ

summary.tldr: PyTorch Helion now integrates NVIDIA CompileIQ to jointly autotune high-level GPU kernel tile configurations and low-level ptxas assembler compiler controls using pre-tuned Advanced Control Files.
key_points: Helion expands autotuning beyond standard Triton parameters (tile shapes, warp counts, pipeline stages) to optimize downstream ptxas machine assembly generation.
NVIDIA CompileIQ tunes ptxas controls—such as register allocation policies, fine-grained instruction scheduling, and code-generation heuristics—and outputs portable Advanced Control Files (ACFs).
Helion's autotuner incorporates CompileIQ's pre-tuned ACF catalogs alongside its existing search space without requiring runtime search overhead for ahead-of-time tuned kernels.
Targeted workloads focus on last-mile performance gains across 27 optimized model kernels, including FP8/NVFP4 quantization, RMSNorm, RoPE, grouped GEMM, and Qwen3 decode layers.
summary.why_it_matters: By exposing lower-level assembler controls to the high-level kernel autotuner, developers can extract extra performance headroom from GPU kernels that are already fully optimized at the PyTorch and Triton levels.

infra.title: How Deepgram optimized voice AI at scale with AWS Trainium

summary.tldr: Deepgram and AWS optimized the Nova-3 speech-to-text model on AWS Trainium2 using PyTorch, achieving 11-70% higher audio throughput per dollar for offline batch workloads.
key_points: Ported Nova-3 to AWS Trainium2 using TorchNeuron and compiled encoder and decoder as separate static-shape graphs via torch.compile with zero CPU fallbacks.
Deployed fused kernels from the Neuron Kernel Interface Library (NKILib) for operations including fused QKV projections, fused FFN layers, and depthwise 1D convolution.
Achieved an optimal deployment running eight model replicas on a single Amazon EC2 trn2.3xlarge instance after sweeping batch sizes from 1 to 128.
Integrated Trainium2 with Deepgram's native model server using a data-parallel Rust runtime.
summary.why_it_matters: This optimization allows high-volume speech AI providers and self-hosting customers to process significantly more batch audio data per dollar without sacrificing model accuracy.

infra.title: Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM

summary.tldr: A new push-based NIXL connector for vLLM disaggregates prefill and decode phases by moving KV cache transfer setup off the critical path, cutting TTFT and TPOT.
key_points: Replaces default pull-based NIXL READ operations with push-based transfers to eliminate consumer-side metadata round trips prior to token generation.
Overlaps decode-instance memory allocation with prefill compute by pre-registering target blocks on the decode side.
Executes NIXL descriptor setup and transfer submission on a dedicated background thread on the prefill instance.
Demonstrated up to a 3x TTFT improvement and up to 30% TPOT reduction using Qwen3-32B on Amazon EC2 P5en instances over AWS EFA.
summary.why_it_matters: Push-based KV transfers remove serialization overhead in disaggregated LLM serving, significantly lowering latency for high-throughput inference workloads.

infra.title: Improve TTFT for multi-turn agentic workloads with bi-directional KV transfer in vLLM

summary.tldr: AWS contributed a bi-directional KV transfer mechanism to vLLM via an enhanced NIXL KV connector, allowing prefill nodes to retrieve decode node KV caches in multi-turn agentic workloads.
key_points: Conventional prefill-decode disaggregation only transfers KV cache from prefill to decode nodes, forcing prefill nodes to recompute KV projections for previously generated model tokens and conversation history on subsequent turns.
Bi-directional KV transfer enables decode nodes to pass stored KV blocks back to prefill nodes, avoiding redundant context recomputation.
The implementation leverages NIXL KV connector enhancements and AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for direct remote memory access (GPUDirect RDMA / Neuron Direct RDMA) across nodes.
Benchmarking on Amazon EC2 P5en instances (1P1D setup) demonstrated TTFT reductions of up to 1.6x for Qwen3-32B and up to 3.3x for zai-org/GLM-5-FP8.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces time to first token (TTFT) and prevents redundant accelerator computation as conversation histories expand in multi-turn LLM agent deployments.

infra.title: Achieving near-zero-downtime scaling in Elastic Expert Parallelism

summary.tldr: vLLM introduced asynchronous preparation and NIXL EP to enable Elastic Expert Parallelism reconfiguration with near-zero downtime during GPU scale-up and scale-down operations.
key_points: Reconfiguration is split into a background preparation phase and a brief commit phase where schedulers pause, reducing scale-up downtime from 100 seconds to 0.82 seconds on 16 to 20 GB200 GPUs.
Scale-down downtime for DeepSeek V4 Pro was reduced from 56 seconds to 1.96 seconds compared to synchronous reconfiguration.
Existing workers use background threads to transfer weights, warm up communication, and sync execution info while continuing to serve using current CUDA graphs.
Asynchronous Expert Parallel Load Balancing (EPLB) redistributes experts in the background after new workers activate and begin handling attention.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows enterprise vLLM deployments to dynamically scale GPU resources for large MoE models like DeepSeek V4 Pro without causing prolonged service interruptions or dropping request SLOs.

infra.title: Structured outputs for Anthropic Claude models on Amazon Bedrock

summary.tldr: Amazon Bedrock now supports native structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models using constrained decoding to enforce JSON Schema compliance.
key_points: Uses constrained decoding during token generation to enforce JSON schema deterministically rather than relying on post-processing.
Available on both bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints, supporting real-time streaming, batch inference, and cross-Region inference.
Validates input against the JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 subset and compiles grammars that are cached per account for 24 hours.
Modifying JSON schema structural fields invalidates the cached grammar, while changing schema names or descriptions retains it.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates JSON parsing exceptions, schema validation code, and retry overhead, enabling lower token usage and reliable production integration.

infra.title: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: 2026 year-to-date in review

summary.tldr: From January through September 2026, Amazon SageMaker JumpStart added over 100 new models from 30 providers, expanding its catalog for one-click deployment, model evaluation, and customization.
key_points: Alibaba led additions with 29 models spanning reasoning (Qwen 3.8-27B), MoE (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B), agents, coding, speech, and embeddings.
NVIDIA contributed 17 models including Cosmos3 world models (Super, Edge, Nano), Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, and Nemotron-3-Super-120B in FP8 and BF16.
Other notable provider onboardings include Mistral (Ministral-3 family, Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime), Google (6 Gemma 4 variants), IBM (Granite 4.0 variants), and Cohere (Command A, Rerank v3.5/v4.0).
Supported customization techniques include LoRA, SFT, DPO, and RLVR with serverless customization options to reduce infrastructure management.
Access is supported via SageMaker Studio, the SageMaker Python SDK, and direct Hugging Face deep links.
summary.why_it_matters: The catalog expansion gives developers streamlined, one-click access and serverless fine-tuning options across a broader range of open-source multimodal, speech, reasoning, and world models.

infra.title: Pegasus 1.5 from TwelveLabs is now available in Amazon Bedrock

summary.tldr: TwelveLabs' Pegasus 1.5 is now available on Amazon Bedrock, enabling structured JSON metadata extraction, multimodal image prompting, and time-based segment tracking for videos up to two hours long without pre-indexing.
key_points: Supports time-based metadata generation and video segmentation for videos up to two hours long using Amazon S3 URIs or base64 strings.
Introduces multimodal prompting combining text with visual reference images to locate specific objects, logos, or persons.
Operates via Amazon Bedrock's InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream APIs under model ID twelvelabs.pegasus-1-5-v1:0 in the us-west-2 region.
Offers two analysis modes via analysisMode parameter: general (text/schema output) and time_based_metadata (structured JSON segment lists with timestamps).
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can now automate deep temporal and visual video analysis directly within AWS infrastructure without needing complex pre-indexing pipelines or fragmented toolchains.

infra.title: GenRecs Tokenization: Transforming Ads Recommendation at Meta with Stable Model Vocabulary

summary.tldr: Meta introduced GenRecs Tokenization, replacing dedicated item IDs with a stable semantic vocabulary to enable generative recommendation models to reason about ad content and user preferences.
key_points: Replaces dedicated entity IDs with a structured, stable semantic token vocabulary across ads, products, pages, and pixels.
Enables zero-shot and cold-start generalization for newly launched ads and niche entities by allowing models to transfer pre-trained world knowledge and insights across campaigns.
Integrates with Meta's Generative Ads Model (GEM) and Adaptive Ranking Model to support both retrieval and ranking production workloads.
Delivered a +0.35% lift in advertiser conversions across Meta surfaces according to internal production measurements from February 2026.
summary.why_it_matters: Semantic tokenization allows recommendation systems to scale with LLM architectures and accurately predict ad relevance even for brand-new entities lacking historical engagement data.
